purpose: Submission plan only: what moves an acceptance decision, in what order, and the pre-registered acceptance test for each. Cell-level mechanism state, closed gaps and the retired v7 ledger live in docs/audit/todo-history.md and docs/audit/todo-archive-2026-10-27.json. The win definition and the decision rule are carried over verbatim; what changed is the ordering rule: work is ranked by how much it moves an acceptance decision, not by which cell is still losing.
objective: The framework must WIN on every model task: R1 (LineageFlow hmmscan hits), R2 (Kanzi RMSD), R3 (FlowMol3 fg_dev), R5a (2D FM W2), R5b (CIFAR FID), R5c (MNIST FID), R6 (LineageFlow scPerplexity/pLDDT), K1 (FlowMol3 pb_validity), K7 (LineageFlow novelty). A TIE is a loss. A LOSS is an open mechanism gap, not a boundary to be published. Every cell that is not a win today has a mechanism gap below whose acceptance test is that win.
submission_objective: Publish in a CAS tier-1 (中科院一区) journal, TNNLS first. The paper is packaged and submittable as of 2026-10-27 (12 pages, 0 overfull, 3 STRONG + 1 CONDITIONAL + 1 TIE + 2 PARTIAL + 4 SUPP-only). What it lacks is not prose but one piece of evidence: the central claim is currently a four-point cross-section, and the reviewer's first objection is already known. The plan below exists to convert that cross-section into an identification, then to put it in the paper.
win_definition: A cell wins only if BOTH hold. (1) POINT WIN: at the cell's canonical protocol (same checkpoint, same N, same seeds), the framework's metric is better with the paired 95% CI excluding 0 and clearing the cell's alpha. (2) FRONTIER DOMINANCE: over the NFE grid, the framework's (quality, NFE) curve lies at or below the baseline's at every grid point, and the framework's plateau is better than the baseline's plateau. (2) is the load-bearing one: flow-matching inference saturates with steps, so 'the baseline with more steps' is NOT a valid control and NOT a threat -- the baseline's ceiling is fixed by its own inference protocol. The framework's claim is that it raises that ceiling AND reaches a given quality at fewer NFE. Both halves are measured, not asserted.
frontier_protocol: Per model: baseline and framework on the SAME checkpoint, prior, seed policy and N, swept over NFE in {10, 25, 50, 100, 200} (extended upward until the baseline plateaus for two consecutive points). Report per-NFE paired deltas with CIs, the plateau estimate (mean of the last two grid points), and the dominance verdict. A cell whose baseline does not plateau on the grid has an unfinished ceiling measurement, not a win.
recording_policy: Observations-only: write audit docs + todo.json + raw artifacts. Frozen CLAIMS.md / CONSOLIDATED_RESULTS.md / paper-A-final.* / tnnls_submission/** stay untouched without explicit user authorization.
decision_rule: An experiment runs only if it can change a claim's STATUS or a metric's MAGNITUDE. More seeds, more draws or a larger N on an already-measured effect do not qualify: they buy confidence, not strength. When a cell is power-limited or negative, stop measuring and strengthen the adapter: study the domain (the upstream implementation, the metric's own definition, the field's validity rules), write the design hypothesis down, change the code, then make ONE pre-registered measurement. A tie is a loss and is treated as an open gap. Seed top-ups after a run are forbidden in every case; a cell's canonical seed set is fixed in its pre-registration before the first number exists.
research_protocol: 1) Read the upstream implementation of the state space being perturbed (channel geometry, latent geometry, embedding geometry) before proposing anything.
2) Read the metric's definition and the scorer, not just its name: what does it reward, and would it reward the change we are about to make for a trivial reason?
3) State the design hypothesis as a falsifiable sentence with the expected sign and rough size, in the audit doc, BEFORE touching code.
4) Change one mechanism at a time; keep the old arm runnable so the before/after is paired on the same seed and the same prior.
5) One confirmatory measurement at the cell's canonical N/NFE/seeds. No seed top-ups afterwards.

6) Never frame the control as 'the baseline with more steps'. Flow-matching inference saturates in the step count, so the baseline's ceiling is set by its own inference protocol; the correct control is the baseline at its plateau, and the claim to prove is (quality, NFE) frontier dominance plus a higher plateau.

venue_assessment.note: Judgment, not measurement. Recorded so the ordering below can be argued with.
venue_assessment.target: IEEE TNNLS (中科院大类 计算机科学 1区; IF 10.2 for 2024; JCR Q1)
drivers_against: the only large effect is on a 5k-step MNIST checkpoint; three better-trained checkpoints tie
no competitive benchmark (MNIST FID 21-24; CIFAR-10 RF FID ~48)
clean cells have small effects (R2 d=-0.099, R1 d=+0.182, R3 d=-0.401 n.s.)
the stated theorems do not predict an FID sign, and the paper says so
engineering bulk (typed contracts, hash ledger, byte-stability) reads as systems work
6 of 7 R-level cells have no (quality, NFE) grid
drivers_for: the framing (control at the round boundary) is genuinely distinct from solver / distillation / alpha-blending
five checkpoint families across protein, molecule, image and toy
reproducibility is far above the norm (30/30 byte-stable vectors, hash-chained ledger, per-cell recipes)
R5c's matched-rung design is sound: same NFE, 7 rungs, 3 seeds, N=1000, dual plateau rule
venue_assessment.timing_risk: TNNLS first review can take 6-12 months. Waiting for reviewer feedback before running GAP-90 therefore risks an 18-24 month total cycle, which is why GAP-90 is ordered first.

open_gaps.status: EXECUTED 2026-10-27 - 42/42 cells, 0 failures, 11m47s on cuda:0 (torch backend)
open_gaps.gap: The paper's central claim is that the gain from re-inference is checkpoint-conditional. The evidence is four MNIST checkpoints presented as a cross-section that differs in architecture, training-set size and training time at once. That framing was wrong on the facts: 5k/10k/60k is a clean training-set dose at fixed width and fixed epoch count, and 60k/epochs2/production is a clean epoch dose at fixed width and fixed training set. Only two of the five dose points have a frontier measurement. A reviewer can accept every number and still reject the inference because the middle of the curve is unmeasured.
open_gaps.design_hypothesis: Under a controlled axis - same architecture, same training set, only the optimizer-step budget varies - the framework's plateau gain decreases monotonically with training completeness, because the gain is the baseline's distance to its own floor (GAP-84 reading). Pre-registered predictions: plateau delta near 0 at 1,874 steps and near 0 at 2,811 steps for both widths; the OLS slope of delta on log(optimizer steps) is positive (gain shrinks as steps grow) with a 95% CI excluding 0; a width-8 checkpoint at production's 2,811 steps agrees with production within 1 FID.
open_gaps.research: 1) No training. Measure the frontier on the two checkpoints that never received one: epochs2 (1,874 steps, width 16) and w8e3 (2,811 steps, width 8). 2) Protocol identical to GAP-84 so the points are comparable: N=1000 per arm, sampling seeds 42/43/44, rungs {4,5,10,25,50,100,200}, --min-steps-per-round 2, headline arm evidence_driven, plateau = mean of the last two rungs, floor rule 1 FID absolute with the 1% relative rule reported alongside, verdict via tools/frontier_report.py unmodified. 3) Combine with GAP-84's four points into one five-level dose curve in optimizer steps plus a two-width comparison at 2,811 steps.
open_gaps.acceptance: All four clauses, or the law is rejected and the manuscript keeps its current hypothesis wording. (a) Across the five optimizer-step levels (78, 156, 937, 1,874, 2,811) the plateau gain is non-increasing and the OLS slope of delta on log(steps) has a 95% CI excluding 0. (b) The 78-step point reproduces the GAP-84 WIN (7/7 strict rungs, plateau CI clearing the floor) - a pipeline consistency check, not new evidence. (c) At 2,811 steps w8e3 and production differ by less than 1 FID in plateau gain. (d) The three 60,000-image points (937/1,874/2,811) all sit inside the floor.
open_gaps.est_wall: a few hours on cuda:0; 84 N=1000 cells (2 checkpoints x 7 rungs x 3 seeds x 2 arms); no training
open_gaps.agent_action: Done. docs/audit/gap90-optsteps-dose.md section 9 holds the per-rung tables, both floor verdicts and the clause-by-clause verdict; section 10 holds the GAP-91 fit. Artifacts: verification_outputs/gap90-optsteps-dose/ (42 cells + frontier_{epochs2,w8e3}_evidence_driven{,_absfloor}.json). Audit correction 2026-10-27 (section 11): re-ran rungs 4 and 5 with --min-steps-per-round 2 on CPU; epochs2 becomes TIE with no violations, so the correct headline is 1 WIN / 5 TIE. Section 12 records two provenance defects and their fixes: sweep_command (370 of 376 distinct cells carried a template string) and commit_sha (540 of 541 cells carried the literal 'PENDING'; now git rev-parse HEAD plus a commit_dirty flag, pinned by tests/test_gap90_provenance_fields.py). Section 12.2 records a third defect that touched GAP-90's own width argument: the size-based smoke flag labelled all 42 w8e3 cells as the 6k-image smoke materialization, contradicting the 2,811-step recipe the width contrast relies on; the flag is now tri-state and the width is read from the weights. Section 13 records two axes checked and not claimable: seed-to-seed sd is not reduced by the framework, and the R5c speed ratio is a cost (1.0-2.5x), not a saving.
open_gaps.result: Plateau delta by optimizer-step budget: 78 -> -3.1206 FID (WIN), 156 -> -1.0036 (TIE), 937 -> +0.0150 (TIE), 1874 -> -0.0037 (TIE under the GAP-84b step cap; the uncapped LOSS is a rung-4 allocation artifact), 2811 width-16 -> -0.0335 (TIE), 2811 width-8 -> -0.2360 (TIE on the 1-FID floor, WIN on a 1% relative floor). The gain collapses to zero between 156 and 937 steps and stays inside the floor. Pre-registered clause (a) monotonicity FAILS strictly (the third step rises by 0.019 FID, 50x below the floor); the OLS slope of delta on log10(steps) PASSES (+1.744, CI [+0.227,+3.260], R2=0.773). Clauses (b), (c), (d) pass. The width-8 result at matched 2,811 steps (0.236 vs 0.034) is not explained by step count and points at baseline quality.

open_gaps.status: EXECUTED IN-FAMILY 2026-10-27 - cross-family hold-out NOT met, relation reported as descriptive
open_gaps.gap: GAP-84 recorded that the gain tracks the baseline's distance to its own floor, but only as a description of four points. A description is a caveat; a predictor is a result.
open_gaps.design_hypothesis: The plateau gain is a function of the baseline plateau's distance to the checkpoint family's floor, and that function predicts the sign and rough size on a checkpoint family it was not fitted on.
open_gaps.research: Fit the relation on the GAP-90 five points plus the four GAP-84 checkpoints; hold out one family (Kanzi reconstruction, or CIFAR-10 FID) and test the prediction there. Report the fit, the held-out error, and the sign agreement.
open_gaps.acceptance: Out-of-sample sign correct on every held-out checkpoint AND |predicted - observed| below 1 FID, the paper's floor unit. Otherwise the relation is reported as descriptive only and the paper says so.
open_gaps.est_wall: no GPU; re-analysis of existing artifacts plus one held-out cell
open_gaps.agent_action: Done as far as the data allow. docs/audit/gap90-optsteps-dose.md section 10 records the fit, the LOO table, the two cautions (non-coupled regression form; x-range 10.0-24.5 with production below the implied fixed point). Do not promote to a cross-family law without a hold-out. Addendum 2026-10-27: tools/gap91_holdout.py reproduces the four-point fit and the two-point hold-out in section 14. Still not a cross-family law; the word 'predicts' stays out of the paper for the interval reason, not the fit reason.
open_gaps.result: framework_plateau = 2.450 + 0.7788 * baseline_plateau; slope CI [0.7282, 0.8293], R2 = 0.9978, n = 6. The framework compresses the quality spread to 78% of the baseline's. Leave-one-out MAE = 0.331 FID, a third of the 1.0 FID floor. The pre-registered hold-out required a second model family; neither candidate has an NFE grid (R2 has none, R5b contrasts round counts at a single NFE=50 budget), so the acceptance clause is NOT met and the manuscript must say 'orders', not 'predicts'. ADDENDUM 2026-10-27 (section 14): a within-family out-of-sample check now exists. Fitting on the four original GAP-84 checkpoints only gives 2.411865 + 0.780448*base (R2 0.99758, slope CI [0.7050,0.8559]) and predicts the two checkpoints added a day later to MAE 0.055 FID (epochs2 -0.098, w8e3 +0.013), against 0.331 for LOO. Both held-out baselines lie inside the training range, so it is interpolation, and the 95% prediction interval at n=4 is +/-1.0 FID, so accuracy is not power. Reproduce: python3 tools/gap91_holdout.py.

open_gaps.status: EXECUTED 2026-10-27 - manuscript insertion done; no GPU
open_gaps.gap: The manuscript states that the two theorems do not determine the sign of an FID change. That is true of the theorems as stated. But GAP-78 measured a contraction (kappa) that does order the sign - 12/12 weak dominance at beta=0.3 on the floor rule - and that measurement is not in the paper.
